findings.question: Which should lead this page for readers in BC? (a) Lung-RADS v2022, by the audit rule (an ACR system; CAR has no lung screening guideline), with a short note on where the BC Cancer Lung Screening Program differs; or (b) the program's own BC Lung Screening Protocol v2.0 (January 2026), which program radiologists report program LDCTs with: PanCan nodule risk score at baseline, volumetry and volume doubling time at follow-up, categories 1–5 (1: back in 2 years; 2: 1 year; 3: repeat LDCT in 3 months; 4–5: the program arranges diagnostic referral), eligibility 55–74 with PLCOm2012 risk ≥ 1.5%, with Lung-RADS as the note? The BC standards never mention Lung-RADS. The page's "Application: Annual" screening also differs from the program's biennial category 1.

recheck.note: Reviewer: outdated. The version, year and publisher are stated correctly for v1.1, but v1.1 was superseded by v2022 in November 2022, so the page presents a retired version as current. (lung-rads-1-1, title, p1; lung-rads-2022, title, p1)
recheck.resolution: Management kept: this is the finding the dated notice hangs on; v2022 changed the stepped management of categories 3 and 4A and added category 0's 1–3 month LDCT, so a reader following v1.1 can get a different interval. The reviewer agrees the page presents a retired version as current.

findings.piece: Calculator: new nodules (New = Yes)
findings.says: With "New nodule on this exam? Yes" the result depends on diameter alone, whatever the nodule type or solid component: runs gave < 4 mm → 3, 4 to < 6 mm → 4A, ≥ 6 mm → 4B. New solid 3.9 → 3 (expected 2), 4.0 and 5.9 → 4A (expected 3), 6.0 and 7.9 → 4B (expected 4A); new part-solid 5.9 mm total → 4A (expected 3), 10 mm with a 3.9 mm solid component → 4B (expected 4A); new ground glass 3.9 → 3, 10.0 and 29.9 → 4B (expected 2), 30.0 → 4B (expected 3).

sources.location: Assessment categories table, p1: category 2 "Solid nodule(s): new < 4 mm"; 3 "new 4 mm to < 6 mm", part solid "new < 6 mm total diameter", non solid "≥ 30 mm on baseline CT or new"; 4A "new 6 to < 8 mm", part solid "with a new or growing < 4 mm solid component"; 4B "new or growing, and ≥ 8 mm", part solid "a new or growing ≥ 4 mm solid component"; non solid < 30 mm is 2 (runs in docs/audit/batch-1/cases/lung_rads.results.md, cases v11-solid-new-*, v11-partsolid-new-*, v11-ggn-new-*: 11 of 13 mismatched)
Lung-RADS v2022 table, p1: the same new-nodule rows; category 2 non solid "< 30 mm … at baseline, new, or growing"

findings.fix: Grade new nodules by type with the v2022 rows: solid < 4 → 2, 4–< 6 → 3, 6–< 8 → 4A, ≥ 8 → 4B; part-solid < 6 mm total → 3, new solid component < 4 → 4A, ≥ 4 → 4B; ground glass < 30 → 2, ≥ 30 → 3. Until then switch the calculator off: it raises every new nodule by a category, and a new 6–29 mm ground-glass nodule to 4B.

recheck.note: The calculator grades every new nodule one category too high (new solid < 4 mm gives 3 not 2, 4 to < 6 mm gives 4A not 3, 6 to < 8 mm gives 4B not 4A) and ignores nodule type, so a new ground-glass nodule of 10 mm returns 4B where the source gives 2. The expected values in the results file agree with the source; the one arguable case is the new 10 mm part-solid nodule with a 3.9 mm solid component (3 or 4A depending on reading), and 4B is wrong on either reading. (lung-rads-1-1, Assessment Categories table, p1, new-nodule criteria in categories 2, 3, 4A, 4B; lung-rads-2022, table p1 (same thresholds))

findings.piece: Calculator: "Additional suspicious features" (4X) field
findings.says: Field "Additional suspicious features? (spiculation, lymphadenopathy, endobronchial lesion)", option "Yes — Apply 4X modifier". Runs: it appends X to the size category: 6 mm solid → "Lung-RADS 3X: Additional suspicious features present — 6-month LDCT Consider chest CT with contrast, PET/CT, and/or tissue sampling." (risk "1-2%"); 8 mm → "Lung-RADS 4AX" (3-month LDCT); 15 mm → "Lung-RADS 4BX". A 5 mm solid nodule with Yes stays "Lung-RADS 2", so a 5 mm endobronchial nodule entered as the hint says gives 2.

sources.location: Assessment categories table, p1, 4X row "Category 3 or 4 nodules with additional features…" sharing the 4B management cell; 4A row "Endobronchial nodule"; Important notes 6 (only the S modifier is added to a category) and 10 (runs in docs/audit/batch-1/cases/lung_rads.results.md, cases v11-4x-solid-6-0, -8-0, -15-0 and v11-endobronchial-5-0 mismatched; v11-4x-solid-5-0 matched)

Notes, p2, note 14 ("4X is a distinct Lung-RADS category; X should not be used as a modifier") and note 11a (segmental or more proximal airway abnormalities are 4A); Lung-RADS v2022 table, p1, 4A "Airway nodule, segmental or more proximal - at baseline" (cases v2022-4x-solid-8-0 and v2022-airway-segmental-5-0 mismatched)

findings.fix: Return "Lung-RADS 4X" with the 4B management when a category 3 or 4 nodule has suspicious features. Take endobronchial lesion out of the hint and make airway nodules their own input (v2022: segmental or more proximal → 4A, subsegmental → 2).

recheck.note: "3X", "4AX" and "4BX" are not Lung-RADS categories: any category 3 or 4 nodule with such features is 4X and is worked up like 4B, yet the calculator keeps the 6-month or 3-month LDCT. An endobronchial nodule is 4A in its own right (v2022: segmental or more proximal), so the 5 mm endobronchial case returning Lung-RADS 2 is an under-call. (lung-rads-1-1, Assessment Categories table, p1, 4X row, 4A "Endobronchial nodule", note 10; lung-rads-2022, notes 11a and 14)

findings.piece: Calculator: branches it has no input for
findings.says: No input for growth, a perifissural/juxtapleural nodule, benign calcification or fat, an airway nodule, an atypical cyst, a stable follow-up or an incomplete exam. It always returns 2, 3, 4A or 4B from size, so it never gives 0 or 1, grades a growing 6 mm solid nodule as 3 and an 8 mm perifissural nodule as 4A (runs v11-solid-baseline-6-0 → 3, v11-solid-baseline-8-0 → 4A).

sources.location: Assessment categories table, p1: category 1 (complete, central, popcorn, concentric ring calcification; fat); 2 (perifissural < 10 mm, note 11; "Category 3 or 4 nodules unchanged for ≥ 3 months"); 4A ("growing < 8 mm"; "Endobronchial nodule"); 4B ("new or growing, and ≥ 8 mm"); note 4 (growth > 1.5 mm)

Lung-RADS v2022 table, p1: juxtapleural nodule (2), airway nodule (2, 4A, 4B), atypical pulmonary cyst (3, 4A, 4B), slow-growing solid or part-solid nodule (4B), stable 3 → 2 and stable 4A → 3; category 0 for inflammatory or infectious findings

findings.fix: Add inputs for at least growth, juxtapleural morphology, benign calcification/fat and airway nodules, or say plainly above the form that it grades size at first detection only and does not apply to growing, juxtapleural, calcified, airway or cystic lesions.

recheck.note: The form has no input for growth, perifissural/juxtapleural morphology, benign calcification or fat, airway nodules, cysts, stability or an incomplete exam, and prints a category from size alone with no caveat. A growing 6 mm solid nodule is 4A in the source (calculator: 3) and an 8 mm perifissural nodule is 2 (calculator: 4A). This is a judgement call between "wrong" and "incomplete"; I chose wrong because the output is a definite category. (lung-rads-1-1, Assessment Categories table, p1, categories 0, 1, 2, 4A and notes 11, 12; lung-rads-2022, table p1, categories 0-4B)

Lung-RADS v2022 table, p1, category 1: "Nodule with benign features: Complete, central, popcorn, or concentric ring calcifications OR Fat-containing"; "12-month screening LDCT"

Lung-RADS v2022 table, p1, category 2 "Juxtapleural nodule: < 10 mm (524 mm3) mean diameter at baseline or new AND Solid; smooth margins; and oval, lentiform, or triangular shape"
p1, I.B Juxtapleural Nodules (peri-fissural, costal pleural, peri-mediastinal and peri-diaphragmatic)

recheck.note: "Perivascular" is in neither version, and the required features (solid, smooth margin, oval/lentiform/triangular shape) are left out, so an 8 mm perivascular or irregular fissural nodule would be called 2 when its size makes it 4A. v2022 widened the rule from perifissural to all juxtapleural nodules. Lung-RADS v2022 table, p1, category 1: "Nodule with benign features"

findings.piece: Category 4A and 4B cards: ground-glass nodules
findings.says: 4A and 4B: "Ground glass (non-solid): No specific size criteria (determined by radiologist judgment)".

sources.location: Assessment categories table, p1: non solid nodules appear only in categories 2 and 3; note 10 (a GGN that doubles in size in 1 year is a 4X feature)
Lung-RADS v2022 table, p1: non solid nodules only in categories 2 and 3; Notes, p2, note 7 (slow-growing GGN stays 2 until it meets another category, e.g. develops a solid component) and note 14

findings.fix: Delete. A ground-glass nodule is 2 (< 30 mm, or ≥ 30 mm stable or slowly growing) or 3 (≥ 30 mm at baseline or new); one that develops a solid component is graded as part-solid, and one that doubles in a year is 4X.

recheck.note: Reviewer: unsourced (management). Neither version has any ground-glass criterion in 4A or 4B, by size or by "radiologist judgment". A pure ground-glass nodule tops out at category 3 by size and reaches category 4 only as 4X (for example doubling in a year) or by developing a solid component. Borderline with "wrong". (lung-rads-1-1, Assessment Categories table, p1, categories 2, 3, 4A, 4B and note 10; lung-rads-2022, table and note 7)
recheck.resolution: Stands as wrong: the page lets a ground-glass nodule be 4A or 4B by 'radiologist judgment', whereas both versions only ever grade a pure ground-glass nodule 2 or 3 (4X aside); that contradicts the source rather than adding to it. The reviewer called it borderline wrong.

Once the lead is decided, cite the version actually followed plus CAR 2019 for management (the "Modifications" line is handled site-wide, B1-guidelines-site-02).
findings.question: Which leads for cystic renal masses? By the rule CAR 2019 leads (it gives the management, Flowchart 4 p. 128), but its Table 1 (p. 131) is the pre-2019 Bosniak classification: CAR searched the literature in March–June 2018 (p. 125) and Bosniak 2019 appeared in June 2019. Bosniak 2019 is endorsed by the Society of Abdominal Radiology, and the 2023 CUA guideline recommends it (Recommendation 2), though its authors say it "will need to be tested prior to widespread clinical implementation". Option A: Bosniak 2019 for the categories and CAR 2019 for management (the IIF schedule is the same in both; CAR adds ultrasound follow-up and urology referral for III/IV), with a short note where CAR's Table 1 differs. Option B: CAR 2019 throughout (pre-2019 classes), with Bosniak 2019 as the difference note. The classes differ on: enhancement (2019 has one definition and lets I/II walls and septa enhance; pre-2019 splits perceived/measurable and sends any measurable enhancement to III/IV); calcification (2019: any type is II; pre-2019: thick/nodular is IIF); hyperattenuating >3 cm (2019: II; pre-2019: IIF); IIF (2019: ≥4 thin or 3 mm enhancing septa/wall, plus heterogeneous T1 hyperintensity on MRI); III/IV (2019 puts ≤3 mm irregular thickening in III and defines a nodule by size and margin); and 2019 alone has MRI criteria and the attenuation-only class II types.

recheck.note: The citation (Radiology 2019;292(2):475-488) and 'CT and MRI' describe the paper correctly, but 'Modifications: None - following published v2019 criteria' is false: the page's criteria (perceived enhancement, 3 cm cut-off for hyperattenuating cysts, thick calcification as IIF, measurable enhancement = III/IV) are the pre-2019 classification of the paper's Table 1, which is also what CAR 2019 Table 1 prints. The page has no MRI criteria at all. Management flag left false because the harm arrives through the content pieces, not the label itself. (bosniak-2019, Table 1 (current classification) vs Table 2 (version 2019); sections 'Bosniak II' and 'Bosniak IIF')

ruling.note: I'd use the. bosniak 2019 criteria and management to supercede CAR since bosniak is newer.

Runs (docs/audit/batch-1/cases/bosniak.results.md): v2019-i-thin-wall-enhancing → III (expected I); v2019-ii-few-septa-enhancing → III (expected II); v2019-iif-many-septa-enhancing → III (expected IIF); v2019-i-thin-wall-equivocal → IIF (expected I); v2019-ii-few-septa-equivocal → IIF (expected II); car2019-ii-few-septa-perceived → IIF (expected II under CAR too).

sources.location: Table 2: class I ("the wall may enhance"), class II type 1 ("septa and wall may enhance"), class IIF ("enhancing" septa/wall); Table 3, Enhancement (single combined definition); section "Proposed Solutions to Interreader Variability…" (enhancing = unequivocally perceived, or ≥20 HU at CT / ≥15% signal intensity at MRI)

findings.fix: Classify by the wall and septa (thin, count, 3 mm, ≥4 mm, irregular, nodule) with enhancement asked of that feature (clearly visible, or ≥20 HU / ≥15% at MRI), so an enhancing thin wall stays I, few thin enhancing septa II and many thin enhancing septa IIF. Even under CAR's pre-2019 table, perceived enhancement of a few thin septa must stay II.

recheck.note: In v2019 enhancement alone never sets the class; wall/septal thickness, number and nodules do. The calculator sends any measurable enhancement to III/IV (thin enhancing wall should be I, 1-3 thin enhancing septa II, >=4 thin enhancing septa IIF) and any 'perceived' enhancement to IIF (should be I or II for a thin wall or few thin septa); v2019 also has no separate 'perceived/equivocal <20 HU' state (not clearly visible and not measurable = nonenhancing). usability.notes: About 80 words before the first field (title, the collapsed reference box's label, the open Quick Reference table). Five fields, three of them dropdowns with 2–3 options, so options are hidden but few. The criteria are on the page without clicks (seven cards below the form), though several are wrong. The form grades size only: no inputs for growth, juxtapleural shape, calcification/fat or airway nodules, and the 4X hint wrongly lists endobronchial lesion.

Page title, heading and the first label, then three number fields; nothing is hidden. The page never states the washout formulas or the 10 HU / 60% / 40% thresholds; they appear only inside a result. The unenhanced field is required, so the relative-washout-only case (no unenhanced scan) cannot be entered.

Sits under the whole washout form. Size and HU are number fields; cancer history is a two-option drop-down. No flowchart: a prose summary follows both calculators (visible without clicking), but it lacks the prior-imaging and 2 cm branches, so neither the calculator nor the text shows ACR's Fig 1.

Short before the form (44 words, the reference box collapsed), but the page is 639 words and states the classes three times (tabbed table, cards, rates table). Five dropdowns (14 options) hide their choices until opened, beside one size box; the classification sits below the form in three tabs, one shown at a time. Enhancement is one answer for the whole mass, not per wall or septum; "Lesion size — required" is not enforced (blank gives II and prints "≤3 cm"); the result names a class and a sentence of management but not the feature that decided it.

46 words before the first field (title, collapsed reference box heading, the at-risk warning, heading). Eight fields, six of them dropdowns, so options are hidden until opened; the APHE dropdown lumps rim APHE with "No". The diagnostic table shows on the default tab below the calculator and the quick-reference table, but the steps before it (LR-TIV, LR-1, LR-2, LR-M) sit behind a "Special Categories" tab and their order is never shown; the table itself is wrong for 10–19 mm. Short page otherwise; the form itself is not wordy.

About 14 words before the size field (title, the collapsed "Reference Information" label, "Fleischner Calculator", the field label); four fields, three of them dropdowns of 2–3 options. The solid table is open below the form, but the subsolid table is behind a tab and the measuring rules in a collapsed box, so half the algorithm is hidden. The size field invites decimals ("e.g., 6.5") and does not say which diameter (average, whole nodule or solid component); there is no solid-component field; risk is asked for subsolid nodules though it is not used; the result is a bare line with no restated inputs, no source cell and no exclusions.
